mainTopic: Defining אָלָל in the משנה, which hard animal parts count as food, and whether certain slaughtered animals need הכשר
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point. Liquids of ערלה are learned from ביכורים through the shared word 'פרי', so only grape and olive liquids count. The גמרא then asks what the משנה's word אָלָל means. רבי יוחנן says it is the neck ligament, and ריש לקיש says it is the bits of meat the knife leaves on the hide. A פסוק in איוב and a ruling of רבי יהודה are each used to challenge one of them. Both challenges are answered by narrowing where the two actually disagree. Next the גמרא asks how leftover meat can only 'join' with other meat, and two אמוראים give a 'part food, part not' case. Then a משנה about a bird's beak and talons, and our משנה's horns, are explained as meaning only their soft, edible parts. Finally רבי אסי rules that certain slaughtered animals need מחשבה and הכשר. The גמרא challenges the הכשר requirement from the rule that food destined for severe טומאה needs no הכשר, and it brings sources for that rule. The last source, from רבי יוסי, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Liquids of ערלה are learned from ביכורים through the word 'פרי'
steps.stepSummary: This last step of the earlier discussion says the rule for liquids of ערלה comes from ביכורים, through the matching word 'פרי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then he learns the rule for ערלה from ביכורים, because the word 'fruit' appears in both places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion. It says the rule for liquids that come from ערלה fruit is copied from the rule of ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word 'פרי' (fruit) both for ערלה and for ביכורים. That shared word links the two topics. So in ביכורים only the liquid of grapes and olives counts like the fruit itself, and in ערלה too a person gets lashes only for drinking the liquid of grapes and olives, not of other fruits.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Fruit; the word shared by both פסוקים
Learning one topic from another because the Torah uses the same word in both
And then he brings it (learns it)

steps.whatToRemember: Only the liquids of grapes and olives get the full status of ערלה fruit. This is learned from ביכורים through the word 'פרי'.

phrases.english: And then he derives it for orla
phrases.notes: He is taking a rule already set for ביכורים and applying it to liquids that come from ערלה fruit.

phrases.english: through 'fruit' and 'fruit', from first fruits.
phrases.notes: ערלה: ויקרא 19:23. ביכורים: דברים 26:2. Both say 'פרי'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the derivation that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ערלה rule for liquids is learned from ביכורים through the word 'פרי', so only grape and olive liquids count.

steps.title: What is the אָלָל mentioned in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the word אָלָל from the משנה and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned 'the אָלָל'. What is אָלָל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a word from the משנה and asks what it means, which sets up the two answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says אָלָל joins together with meat to make up the egg-size amount for food טומאה, even though it is not really food on its own. Before we can apply that rule, we need to know what part of the animal אָלָל is.

keyTerms.meaning: A word from the משנה for some part of the animal that is not real food but joins with meat
What?

phrases.english: And the alal.
What is alal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: explaining a word in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What part of the animal the word אָלָל refers to

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says neck ligament; ריש לקיש says meat left on the hide
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אָלָל is the neck ligament (מרטקא). ריש לקיש says it is the meat the knife leaves stuck to the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it is the neck ligament. ריש לקיש said: it is meat that the knife left behind.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different answers to what אָלָל means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says it is the tough ligament in the neck. ריש לקיש says it is the small pieces of meat still stuck to the hide after skinning. Both are things that are not quite real food, so either fits the משנה's rule that אָלָל only 'joins' with meat.

keyTerms.meaning: The neck ligament, a tough band of tissue in the back of the neck
Meat the knife 'spit out', meaning bits of meat left on the hide when skinning

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: the neck ligament,
and Reish Lakish says:
meat that the knife has 'spit out'.
phrases.notes: He means the bits of meat left stuck to the hide after the animal is skinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with two opinions
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: neck ligament. ריש לקיש: meat left on the hide by the knife.

steps.title: Challenge from איוב: 'רופאי אליל' means something that can't be healed
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in איוב calls useless advisors 'רופאי אליל'. That fits a ligament that cannot heal. It does not fit loose meat, which can heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a פסוק: 'But you are plasterers of lies, you are all healers of אליל.' This works well for the one who says it is the neck ligament, since that cannot be healed. But for the one who says it is meat left by the knife, that can be healed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's explanation using a פסוק in איוב that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב insults his friends by calling them 'healers of אליל', meaning doctors trying to fix something that cannot be fixed. A neck ligament cannot heal, so רבי יוחנן's meaning fits. Meat hanging from the hide can heal, so according to ריש לקיש the insult makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Plasterers of lies, people who cover things over with falsehood
Healers of something worthless or unhealable
It works well for... (opens a contrast that leads to a problem)
Able to be healed

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is only against ריש לקיש. רבי יוחנן's explanation fits the פסוק perfectly.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'But you are plasterers of lies,'
'you are all physicians of no value.'
phrases.notes: The word אֱלִל here is the same word as אָלָל in the משנה.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says the neck ligament,
that is why it says this, since it cannot be healed,
but according to the one who says
meat that the knife has 'spit out',
that can be healed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: ״וְאוּלָם אַתֶּם טֹפְלֵי שָׁקֶר רֹפְאֵי אֱלִל כֻּלְּכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's definition from step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's definition of אָלָל as meat left on the hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses אליל for something that cannot heal. Meat on the hide can heal, so that cannot be the meaning of the word.

steps.title: Everyone agrees about the פסוק; they argue only about the משנה's word
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that the אליל in the פסוק is the neck ligament. The dispute is only about what the משנה means by אָלָל.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the אָלָל of the פסוק, everyone agrees. Where they argue is about the אָלָל of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the פסוק and the משנה do not have to use the word in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees that in איוב the word means the neck ligament, which cannot heal. But he holds that the חכמים in the משנה used אָלָל for the meat left on the hide. So the פסוק does not disprove him.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the פסוק
Everyone, meaning both sides of the dispute
They disagree
Our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: In the פסוק, אליל means the neck ligament according to everyone. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue only about the word אָלָל in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: a word in the language of the חכמים can mean something different from the same word in תנ"ך.

phrases.english: Regarding the alal of the verse,
everyone agrees, there is no dispute;
phrases.notes: Both agree that in the פסוק it means the neck ligament.

phrases.english: where they disagree is about the alal of the mishnah.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּאָלָל דִּקְרָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the dispute: the פסוק and the משנה use the word differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק uses אליל for something that cannot heal, the משנה's אָלָל must mean the same thing, which would disprove ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees about the פסוק. ריש לקיש holds that the משנה uses אָלָל for meat left on the hide.

steps.title: Bringing רבי יהודה's ruling about gathered אָלָל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה: gathered אָלָל of an olive-size in one place makes one liable. רב הונא adds that this applies only when a person gathered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: אָלָל that was gathered together, if there is an olive-size in one place, one is liable for it. And רב הונא said: this is only when he gathered it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to test the two definitions of אָלָל. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats gathered אָלָל like real נבלה meat once there is a כזית together. רב הונא adds that a person must have gathered it himself. By doing that, he shows he treats it as something to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: gathered together
an olive-size, the basic amount for liability
that he (a person) gathered it

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The alal that was gathered together,
if there is an olive-size in one place,
one is liable for it,
phrases.notes: He means it carries the טומאה of נבלה, like the meat itself.

phrases.english: and Rav Huna said: that is only when he gathered it.
phrases.notes: A person gathered it on purpose. That shows he treats it as food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the פסוק in איוב, the גמרא tests the two definitions of אָלָל against a ruling of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of רבי יוחנן (אָלָל = neck ligament)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only brings the source. The attack itself comes in the next step.

steps.title: A ligament is like wood, so why would an olive-size matter?
steps.stepSummary: The ruling fits ריש לקיש, since loose meat can be food. But according to רבי יוחנן, a ligament is just like wood, so an olive-size of it should mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine according to the one who says אָלָל is the meat the knife left behind. That is why one is liable when there is an olive-size. But according to the one who says it is the neck ligament, so what if there is an olive-size? It is just wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for an olive-size only makes sense for something that counts as food. Loose meat counts, so ריש לקיש's view fits. A hard ligament is not food at all, so רבי יוחנן's view seems to clash with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: just wood, meaning not food at all
so what? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: It is fine according to the one who says
it is the meat the knife left behind,
that is why when there is an olive-size, one is liable.
But according to the one who says it is the neck ligament,
when there is an olive-size, so what?
It is just wood!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּשָׂר שֶׁפְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source quoted in step 6 to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's definition of אָלָל as the neck ligament
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An olive-size makes one liable only for food. A ligament is like wood, so רבי יהודה cannot be talking about a ligament.

steps.title: The dispute is only about the view of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that רבי יהודה's אָלָל is loose meat. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue only about the רבנן: does the ligament also join in with the meat?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה they do not argue. Where they argue is according to the רבנן. רבי יוחנן said: the ligament also joins in. ריש לקיש said: only the meat the knife left behind joins in, but the ligament does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the argument away from רבי יהודה to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, who makes one liable for an olive-size, both agree that אָלָל means loose meat. Their real argument is about the רבנן's list of things that join together with meat. רבי יוחנן says the ligament joins too, and ריש לקיש says only loose meat does.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the view of
they do not argue
the Sages (the majority view)
joins together to make up the needed amount
only, specifically

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן changed his mind. He agrees only that רבי יהודה's אָלָל is loose meat. For the רבנן he still holds that the ligament counts too.
steps.whatToRemember: Both agree on רבי יהודה's אָלָל (loose meat). They argue only about the רבנן: רבי יוחנן says the ligament also joins, and ריש לקיש says only loose meat joins.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, they do not argue;
where they argue is according to the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַרְטְקָא נָמֵי מִצְטָרֵף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: the ligament also joins in,
phrases.notes: It joins with the meat to reach the amount needed to become טמא as food.

phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said:
only the meat the knife left behind joins in,
but the ligament does not join in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing where the dispute applies: it is moved from רבי יהודה's view to the view of the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוחנן's definition also applies to the אָלָל of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, both agree it is loose meat. For the רבנן, they argue whether the ligament also joins in.

steps.title: When can loose meat only 'join in'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the 'joining' of loose meat is talking about. If a person treats it as food, it becomes טמא even alone. If he does not, he has cancelled it as food completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: This meat the knife left behind, what is the case? If he thinks of it as food, it becomes טמא even by itself. And if he does not think of it as food, he has completely cancelled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty about the rule that loose meat 'joins together' with the meat. It shows that both possible cases seem to leave no room for the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something 'joins in' only if it is not enough by itself but still counts a little. If the owner plans to eat the leftover meat, it is full food and needs no joining. If he does not plan to eat it, it is not food at all and should not even join. So 'joining' seems to have no case where it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? What are the details?
he has in mind to use it as food
by itself, on its own
he has completely cancelled it (as food)

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בָּשָׂר שֶׁפְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: This meat the knife left behind, what is the case?
If he thinks of it as food,
it becomes impure even by itself;
and if he does not think of it as food,
he has completely cancelled it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי בָּשָׂר שֶׁפְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 8 placed the dispute in the רבנן's rule of 'joining'. Now the גמרא questions how loose meat can 'join' at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that meat left behind by the knife joins together with the meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided trap: if he means to eat it, it is full food and needs no joining. If he does not, it is not food and cannot join. Neither case fits the rule.

steps.title: First answer: he planned to eat only part of it
steps.stepSummary: One of the two אמוראים explains that the person intended to eat some part of the loose meat, but we do not know which part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין and רבי מיישא answered. One said: he intended to eat part of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question from Step 9: how can loose meat be food enough to join, but not food enough to become טמא alone? The first answer is that he planned to eat only part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said there are only two choices: either he treats it as food, or he cancels it completely. This answer gives a middle case. He treats part of it as food, but we do not know which part. So no single piece can be called food by itself, but the part he wants to eat can join with the meat to reach a כביצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of it, here meaning part of the loose meat
He intended it, meaning he planned to eat it as food

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin and Rabbi Meyasha:
One said: he intended to eat part of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַבִּי מְיָישָׁא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the either/or question of Step 9 by giving a middle case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle case between full food and fully cancelled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either all of it is food and becomes טמא alone, or none of it is food and it cannot join.
steps.terutzMaskana: He intended to eat an unknown part, so it only joins and does not become טמא alone.

steps.title: Second answer: part torn by an animal, part cut by a knife
steps.stepSummary: The other אמורא says some of the loose meat was torn off by an animal and some was cut by a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: part of it was torn off by an animal, and part of it was cut off by a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The second אמורא gives a different middle case. Part of the meat stayed on the hide because an animal tore it, and part because a knife cut it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat left on the hide when he cut with a knife is meat he left behind on purpose, so he cancelled it as food. Meat that an animal tore off was never cancelled, so it is still food. Since we do not know which part is which, it cannot become טמא by itself, but the animal-torn part joins with the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut it off or tore it away, leaving it attached to the hide
A wild animal
A knife

phrases.english: And one said:
An animal tore off part of it,
and a knife cut off part of it.

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers give a 'part food, part not' case. Since we cannot tell which piece is which, the loose meat only joins with other meat. It does not become טמא by itself.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a mixed case based on how the meat was separated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loose meat must be either all food or all cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal-torn part is food and the knife-cut part is cancelled, and since they are mixed it only joins.

steps.title: A משנה about a bird's beak and talons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in טהרות saying a bird's beak and talons become טמא, make things טמא, and join with the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: the beak and the talons become impure, make other things impure, and join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה from another place. It is setting up a question about the beak in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said hard parts like horns can join with meat. This other משנה says the same about a bird's beak and talons. They can become טמא, pass on טומאה, and join with the meat to reach the size that makes food טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird's beak
Claws or talons
They become טמא and they make other things טמא

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in טהרות 1:2.

phrases.english: The beak and the talons
become impure, and make impure, and join together.
phrases.notes: They join with the bird's meat to make the size needed for food טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic connected to the horns in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird's beak and talons can become טמא, make things טמא, and join with the meat.

steps.title: But a beak is just wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a beak can count as food when it is as hard as wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A beak is just wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה it just quoted. A beak is not food at all, so how can it join?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only food can become טמא with food טומאה or join to make up food size. A beak is hard and nobody eats it, so it is like wood. That seems to go against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Just wood, meaning it is not food at all

phrases.english: A beak is merely wood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the beak joins and becomes טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that is not food cannot have food טומאה. A beak is like wood, so it should not count.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: it means the lower beak
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is talking about the lower half of the beak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: it is talking about the lower beak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by narrowing the משנה to the lower part of the beak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He suggests the משנה does not mean the whole beak, only the lower part of it. The next step questions this, because the lower part seems just as hard.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower one, here the lower part of the beak

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: it is talking about the lower beak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows which part of the beak the משנה means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה means the whole hard beak.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only the lower beak.

steps.title: The lower beak is also wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the lower beak is just as hard and inedible.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lower one is also just wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר. The lower beak is hard too, so the same question comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'lower beak' does not solve anything if that part is also not food. The question from Step 13 applies to it in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: The lower one is also merely wood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's answer in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's answer that the משנה means the lower beak.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lower beak is just as hard and inedible, so it has the same problem.

steps.title: רב פפא: the underside of the upper beak
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רבי אלעזר meant the lower side of the upper beak, the soft part inside the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it means the lower part of the upper beak.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains what 'lower' really means. It is not the lower jaw. It is the soft underside of the upper beak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The underside of the upper beak, inside the mouth, has a soft layer stuck to it. That soft part counts as food, so it can become טמא and join with the meat. This answers the question that a beak is just wood.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower side of the upper beak, the soft part inside the mouth
The upper one

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תַּחְתּוֹן שֶׁל עֶלְיוֹן.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: the lower part of the upper one.
phrases.notes: He means the soft part on the inside of the upper beak, facing into the mouth.

steps.whatToRemember: A beak, like wood, is not food. The משנה's beak that joins is the soft underside of the upper beak, which does count as food.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תַּחְתּוֹן שֶׁל עֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by explaining what 'lower' means in רבי אלעזר's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what רבי אלעזר's words mean.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lower beak' means the lower jaw, which is hard like wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the soft underside of the upper beak, which counts as food.

steps.title: The talons mean the part buried in the flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the talons in the משנה refer to the part sunk into the flesh, not the hard claw itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: About talons, רבי אלעזר said: the משנה means the spot that is buried in the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the same problem for talons that it just solved for the beak. Hard claws are not food, so רבי אלעזר says the משנה means only the soft base inside the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talons raise the same difficulty as the beak: something hard cannot count as food. רבי אלעזר limits the משנה to the base of the talon, which is soft and attached to the meat. That part can sensibly become טמא as food and join with the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Talons or claws
Buried or sunk into something
Flesh or meat

phrases.english: Talons: Rabbi Elazar said:
The place that is buried in the flesh.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Both mean the same here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same approach as the beak answer and applies it to the talons
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a soft, edible part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Talons, like the beak, seem too hard to count as food
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means the soft base of the talon that is buried in the flesh

steps.title: The horns mean the place that bleeds when cut
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that horns count as food only at the spot where cutting them makes blood come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: About horns, רב פפא said: the משנה means the place where, when you cut, blood comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא handles horns in the same way. The hard horn is not food, so רב פפא limits the rule to the soft, living base where cutting draws blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of a horn is dead, hard material, like wood. Near the base it is still living tissue, so cutting there makes it bleed. That living part is close enough to meat to count as food for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Horns
Cutting
Blood

phrases.english: Horns: Rav Pappa said:
In the place where one cuts
And blood comes out of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of answer to horns
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a soft, living part
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Horns are hard and should not count as food
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the base of the horn, which bleeds when cut, counts
steps.whatToRemember: Hard parts like the beak, talons and horns count as food only at their soft parts: the inside of the upper beak, the base of the talon inside the flesh, and the base of the horn that bleeds.

steps.title: Back to our משנה: one who slaughters an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה about slaughtering an animal, to discuss it next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Similarly, one who slaughters an animal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to our own משנה and quotes the words 'similarly, one who slaughters an animal.' This is a setup line that opens a new topic, and רבי אסי explains it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that an animal slaughtered this way, while it is still twitching, can become טמא as food but not as a נבלה. The גמרא quotes only the opening words, which works like a heading. The explanation comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly, in the same way
One who slaughters
An animal

phrases.english: Similarly, one who slaughters an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טהרות discussion and returns to our משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of slaughtering an animal, to be explained next

steps.title: רבי אסי: two cases that need intent and outside water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says the משנה covers a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal and a גוי slaughtering a kosher one. Both need מחשבה and הכשר from water that comes from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: They teach this about a Jew with a non-kosher animal and a גוי with a kosher animal. They need intent to use it as food, and they need to be made susceptible by water from another place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי explains which cases the משנה is talking about. He says that in these cases the meat only becomes able to receive food-טומאה if two things happen: someone intends it as food, and it gets wet from water that comes from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it is made 'ready' (הכשר) by a liquid. Something not normally eaten also needs a thought to use it as food (מחשבה). רבי אסי says this twitching meat needs both, and the הכשר cannot come from the blood of this slaughter. It must be water from another place.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal
A kosher animal
Intent, here a thought to use something as food
Making food able to receive טומאה by getting it wet
From another place, from an outside source

steps.confusionAlert: Here טמאה and טהורה mean non-kosher and kosher animals. They do not mean ritually impure and pure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
They teach: a Jew with a non-kosher animal,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule covers this case: a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: And a gentile with a kosher animal –
They need intent
And being made susceptible by water from another place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: שׁוֹנִין יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּטְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה line quoted in step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal or a גוי slaughtering a kosher animal, the meat needs מחשבה and הכשר from outside water before it can receive food-טומאה
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that food-טומאה needs two separate conditions here, intent and wetting. The blood of this slaughter does not count as the wetting.

steps.title: Why would this animal need הכשר at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי: food that will one day carry a severe impurity does not need הכשר, so why should these animals need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need הכשר? This animal will one day become impure with a severe impurity, and anything that will one day carry a severe impurity does not need הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the end of רבי אסי's statement, the part that says the animal needs הכשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally food only becomes able to pick up impurity after water touches it. That step is called הכשר. But there is a rule that food destined for a stronger impurity skips this step. The flesh of an animal can one day carry the severe impurity of a carcass, so הכשר should not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A severe, stronger level of impurity, like the impurity of a carcass
It will eventually become impure, meaning it is destined for that impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two requirements. מחשבה means thinking of the item as food. הכשר means water touching it. The question here is only about הכשר.

phrases.english: Why do I need הכשר?
It will eventually become impure with a severe impurity,
and anything that will eventually become impure with a severe impurity
does not need הכשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הכשר requirement in רבי אסי's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that both animals need הכשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food destined for severe impurity doesn't need הכשר. An animal's flesh is destined for the severe impurity of a carcass, so it should not need הכשר.

steps.title: The source: seeds need הכשר because they never get severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק about water on seeds that only food never destined for severe impurity needs הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches: 'But if water is put upon the seed.' Seeds will never carry a severe impurity, and they need הכשר. So too, anything that will never carry a severe impurity needs הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the rule it just used comes from: a teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that teaches הכשר speaks about seeds. Seeds can never carry a severe impurity, so the rule of הכשר applies only to foods like them. Food that can carry a severe impurity, like meat, is not like seeds and does not need הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeds or produce, the example the פסוק uses for הכשר
'Just as ... so too', a way of building a comparison from one case to others like it

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the limits of הכשר. It applies only to food that is never destined for severe impurity, which is the basis of the challenge to רבי אסי.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael teaches:
"But if water is put upon the seed",
Just as seeds, which will never
become impure with a severe impurity, need הכשר,
so too anything that will never
become impure with a severe impurity needs הכשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule used in the challenge
steps.raayaObject: The rule that food destined for severe impurity does not need הכשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל on ויקרא 11:38

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks why a kosher bird's carcass needs no הכשר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי asks why נבלת עוף טהור needs מחשבה but not הכשר. His reason begins but is cut off here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: רבי יוסי said: Why did they say that the carcass of a kosher bird needs מחשבה but does not need הכשר? Because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that seems to follow the same rule. It is setting up רבי יוסי's reason, which comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher bird's carcass is a case where the law says no הכשר is needed. רבי יוסי is about to explain why, and his reason will connect to the rule about severe impurity. Only the question and the first word of the answer appear here.

keyTerms.meaning: The carcass of a kosher bird that died without proper שחיטה
For what reason

phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
For what reason did they say
that the carcass of a kosher bird needs intention
but does not need הכשר?
Because

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source that seems to follow the same principle about severe impurity and הכשר
steps.raayaObject: The principle that food destined for severe impurity does not need הכשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי about נבלת עוף טהור
